definition: Brave Leo is a large language model-based chatbot developed by Brave Software and built into the Brave browser.
details: Marketed as a privacy-preserving assistant, Leo can summarize and translate web pages, answer questions about page content, generate text and code, and hold conversational exchanges, all from the browser's address bar or sidebar.

explainer.lead: Brave Leo is a chatbot built into the Brave browser by Brave Software. It brings page summaries, translations, questions, writing, and code generation into the browser, with privacy presented as a central feature.

tiers.eli5: Leo is like a helper sitting beside you while you read a webpage. You could open a long article and ask, “What are the main points?”, and Leo would give you a shorter summary. You can also ask it to translate the page, explain something on it, write text, or help with code.
tiers.practitioner: Use Leo through Brave’s address bar or sidebar to summarize or query page content, translate pages, draft text, generate code, or continue a conversation. Validate generated answers and code before relying on them. Brave’s privacy-preserving positioning should not be treated as a specification of data handling or model architecture.
tiers.paperLevel: At the product level, Leo can be described as response = LLM(user request, optional webpage context), operating through browser address-bar and sidebar interfaces. Supported tasks include summarization, translation, page-grounded question answering, text and code generation, and dialogue. Its architecture, training data, parameter count, and formal evaluation results are not specified.

components.name: Browser entry points
components.detail: The address bar and sidebar let the user make requests without leaving Brave.

components.name: Webpage context
components.detail: Page content can supply the material for summaries, translations, and answers.

components.name: Language-model chatbot
components.detail: The large language model-based assistant produces answers, text, code, and conversational replies.

flow: The user opens Leo from Brave’s address bar or sidebar.
Leo receives a request, optionally together with content from the current webpage.
The language-model chatbot processes the request and page context.
Leo returns a summary, translation, answer, generated text or code, or conversational reply.
explainer.origin: Brave Leo was developed by Brave Software and integrated into the Brave browser.
explainer.whyItMatters: Leo places language-model assistance directly alongside web browsing, reducing the need to move page content into a separate chatbot. Its privacy-preserving positioning also makes data handling a prominent part of the product’s appeal.
